questions.q: What is the result of adding (-3) + (-4) on a number line?
questions.a: The result is -7. A wrong answer like +7 or +1 reveals that the student is ignoring the negative signs and treating them as regular addition or failing to move in the correct direction on the number line.

questions.q: If you are at Floor +2 and you press the "-3" button in the lift, explain why you end up at Floor -1.
questions.a: Starting at +2, moving down 3 floors takes you past 0 (the ground) to -1. A student who says the answer is +1 or -5 has not grasped that negative movement from a positive starting point crosses the zero barrier.

questions.q: Evaluate: (+5) + (-8). Show your steps using the token method.
questions.a: Place 5 green (positive) tokens and 8 red (negative) tokens. Pair each green with a red to form 5 "zero pairs" (which equal 0). You are left with 3 red tokens, so the answer is -3. A common error is to just subtract the numbers and guess the sign; the token method proves the sign must be negative because more negatives exist.

questions.q: Compare the addition of (+3) + (+5) and (+3) + (-5). How does the "direction" of the second number change the final result?
questions.a: Adding +5 moves you further away from zero in the positive direction (reaching +8), while adding -5 moves you backward, crossing zero and landing in the negative side (reaching -2). A wrong answer suggests the student thinks the sign of the second number doesn't matter for the final direction.

questions.q: Is it possible for the sum of a positive integer and a negative integer to be zero? Provide an example.
questions.a: Yes, when the numbers are additive inverses, such as (+4) + (-4) = 0. Students who say "no" do not yet understand that positive and negative quantities can perfectly cancel each other out.

questions.q: Create a real-world word problem that results in the expression (-10) + (+15).
questions.a: A valid problem would be: "I owed a shopkeeper ₹10 (represented as -10), but then I earned ₹15 and paid him back (represented as +15). What is my new balance?" A poor answer would be a problem that doesn't involve a starting debt or negative state.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Adding integers is the process of combining two numbers that include positive values, negative values, or zero, often ______ as movement along a number line or floor changes in a building.
Fill in the blank: If you are at the ground floor of a ______ and someone tells you to go up 3 floors and then down 5 floors, where do you end up?
What is Adding integers? State the definition given in this lesson.
questions.a: Adding integers is the process of combining two numbers that include positive values, negative values, or zero, often visualized as movement along a number line or floor changes in a building.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: You will land on -______, which is your new position.
What common mix-up does this lesson flag about Adding integers?
questions.a: Students often confuse the sign of the sum when adding a positive and a negative number.

questions.q: What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: The student must be able to accurately calculate the sum of any two integers (positive or negative) using a number line or the "zero pair" token method.
